prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S521: The Airline Operations Coordinator confirms whether the aircraft can remain on plan, accept a short readiness deferral, or require a revised departure intent.
S522: The Handling Resource Planner assigns a severity level to the handler exception and suppresses duplicate updates while the accountable party is still working the same recovery action.
S523: The Ground Handling Dispatcher sends the Towbar Shortage Report when towbar availability cannot support the agreed pushback sequence.
S524: Towbar availability is escalated only when the missing equipment affects a flight inside the active departure planning horizon or blocks a higher-priority aircraft movement.
S525: The Ramp Movement Board displays the resulting constraint as a stand-level exception with a time band rather than as a continuous stream of equipment messages.
S526: Handler exceptions include staffing gaps, equipment unserviceability, access limitations, and service sequencing conflicts that could invalidate a readiness milestone.
S527: The Airport CDM Portal keeps detailed handler notes available to authorized users while the Common Situation Display shows only the flight impact, severity, and expected recovery window.
S528: This separation prevents local troubleshooting details from crowding the regional view used by the Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, and Slot Coordinator.
S529: The Alert Distribution Hub routes notifications according to severity, time to milestone, and subscribed operational role, rather than broadcasting every exception to all users.
S530: A baggage or handler exception becomes a coordination issue when it threatens the Target Off Block Time, the Calculated Takeoff Time, or an agreed runway metering sequence.
S531: At that point, the Airport CDM Portal prompts the accountable role to record the proposed mitigation in the Collaborative Decision Log.
S532: The Regional Flow Manager sees aggregated impact by departure bank, runway stream, and airline group instead of individual baggage or handler work items.
S533: The Slot Allocation Engine uses the sanitized readiness state when evaluating whether a regulated flight can keep its allocated departure opportunity.
S534: The Departure Metering Service applies exception status only after the Business Rules Registry threshold confirms that the condition is operationally material.
S535: Nightjar shall suppress handler-exception annotations for arriving flights unless the exception changes the Airport Acceptance Rate or a regulated arrival sequence.
S536: The Tower Sequence Manager receives a stable readiness indicator and an escalation flag, which allows tower planning to continue without interpreting ramp work details.
S537: The Audit Event Ledger records who raised, changed, acknowledged, or closed each escalated exception so that later review can distinguish data noise from operational decisions.
